name: Rifts DS
english_description: A Dead Souls 3.9 lineage mudlib (same ds386/dsI/dsII/dsIII/dshakkard/deadsouls_fluffos engine family) reskinned onto Palladium's post-apocalyptic Rifts tabletop RPG setting (P.P.E./M.D.C.-flavored stats, Rifts-specific races including a custom greathorneddragon race). Not a duplicate of the already-onboarded rifts2 (DarkeLIB/Nightmare lineage, unrelated codebase, same tabletop setting only). Arrives as a live/played development snapshot (pre-existing wizard accounts and save data, not a fresh archive) rather than a pristine install. SEVERE FINDING: the repo's own flagship-looking content -- domains/omega (150 files describing a detailed multi-floor sci-fi space station, 'Omega Station') plus domains/common (33 files of shared sci-fi item/ship infrastructure) plus the bundled domains/std Lima-style builder-school example area (315 files, part of stock Dead Souls 3.9 itself) -- depends entirely on base-object classes (LIVING, M_VENDOR, CONTAINER, M_OPENABLE, M_WEARABLE, M_GETTABLE, ARMOUR, INDOOR_ROOM, ELEVATOR, KEY, OBJ, PARAM_OBJ, BOOK, VEHICLE, ADVERSARY, STOCK_MASTER, RANGED_WEAPON) that are never defined anywhere in the repository (checked the full mudlib tree, the bundled driver source, and the non-mudlib extra/ directory). None of it compiles; confirmed both via a full lpcc_check.sh sweep (496 of 519 total failures trace to this one root cause) and live via an admin goto into the omega elevator room, which throws the same inherit-error interactively. This was not invented or introduced by conversion -- secure/include/compat.h shows the repo's own author was mid-way through building a compat shim for exactly this purpose (COMPAT_MODE is live and correctly maps ~50 other verb/class names) but never finished it; the upstream git history (10 commits total) reads as abandoned mid-development. Documented per AGENTS.md #7.164 rather than reconstructed (authoring the missing framework would mean inventing a second mudlib engine, not fixing a bug). The lib's REAL functional content is the stock Dead Souls 3.9 base plus its thin continent-domain stubs (Africa/Americas/Atlantis/Australia/AustraliaOutback/China/Europe/Japan/Mexico/Russia/SouthAmericas) and the standard campus/town/Praxis/Ylsrim/default/amigara demo areas, all of which compile and play cleanly. Found and fixed 8 real programming bugs during onboarding: the MudOS 'TYPE array NAME' idiom (230+ single-declarator + 11 multi-declarator instances, including a class-typed variant new to AGENTS.md #7.163), the .c-to-.lpc filename-slice-length bug (AGENTS.md #7.118-class, several sites), a mis-decoded Latin-1/Cyrillic word list in secure/sefun/translate.lpc (same file ds386 also hit), a narrow SetLong(string) vs mixed-closure type mismatch in lib/std/room.lpc, a wrong-declared-type local variable in lib/player.lpc's Setup() (RemoveExtraChannels crash on every login), a stray doubled quote in domains/town/npc/zoe.lpc breaking the bank room's compile, and the same set_pre_exit_functions/SetProperty macro-arity bug already catalogued from ds386's sibling Praxis/supply2.lpc. Also ported ~160 already-proven ds386 driver-compat fixes (uid stubs, OLD_ED editor rewrite, economy int/float truncation, runtime_config.h slot mismatch, etc.) directly since large parts of this lib's shared engine tree are byte-identical to ds386's own pre-fix baseline. See libs/riftsds/NOTES.md and AGENTS.md #7.163/#7.164 for the full writeup.
